utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Judge Fluegge is for urgent personal reasons unable to sit today and the coming days. However, it -- it's expected we have short duration, that is, this week, which is three working days left. Judge Moloto and myself have considered whether it would be in the interests of justice to continue to hear this case and we concluded that it is. Therefore, we'll sit 15 bis today and the coming days. If the Defence is ready to call its next witness, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. Slavoljub Mladjenovic is our next witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to deal with a matter related to this witness. On the 20th of February of this year, the Rule 92 ter motion for Witness Mladjenovic was filed. Considering the change in his mode of testimony from 92 ter to viva voce, the Chamber hereby declares the Rule 92 ter motion of this witness moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you. Could you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Mladjenovic. Mr. Mladjenovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the usual procedure in this courtroom, could you please slowly state your name and surname.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Slavoljub Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, could you please tell us where and when you were born.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of January [As interpreted], 1961, in Ljubovija, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just repeat the date of your birth, because it seems to me that the record does not reflect exactly what you had said.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 6th of June, 1961, in Ljubovija, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where do you live today?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Today I live in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court about your professional qualifications and your education.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I completed elementary school in Bratunac. Secondary school in Ljubovija; it was a general high school, a gymnasium. Then also in Belgrade, I completed my post-secondary education in the field of physical education, and also I got my university degree from the University of Sarajevo in Pale, in physical education as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the job you have today?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Right now, I am the director of the public library in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, do you have any kind of military education or training?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. In 1980, I did my regular military service in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992, where did you happen to be?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: After I completed my post-secondary education, I worked as a PE teach in Prnjavor, Fakovici, in Bjelovac near Bratunac; that is to say, when the war broke out, I was the director of the elementary school in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any kind of military involvement at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Until the 17th of April, no. The 17th of April, 1992. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, on the 17th of April, 1992, I was called up by the Territorial Defence to report to the village of Krasan [Realtime transcript read in error "Krasim"] Polje, where my parents lived, to report to the Territorial Defence. That's where I belonged. The TO of Krasanpolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Krasanpolje, did it have a mixed ethnic composition or was it a single ethnicity living there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What were the ethnic communities living there in Krasanpolje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: In Krasanpolje there were Serbs and Muslims. There were a bit more Serbs though.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What were your tasks at that point in time as a member of the Territorial Defence in the village of Krasanpolje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My task was to have the TO Krasanpolje form -- I mean, those who were military age and able bodied, I mean, we should provide security for the village. However, at first we had village guards, village patrols together with the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies to interrupt. I just saw on the transcript that the name of the village is spelled Krasim Polje, and I'm wondering if that is the correct spelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not the first time. It's the second time I think it's spelled that way. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I see that. And I see in line 9 on page 4 that marking that means that there is no certainty as far as the toponym is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Mladjenovic, for the record I would like to ask you to state slowly the name of the village where you had these military duties then.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Krasanpolje.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: K-r-a-s-a-n.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the situation like in Bratunac and Krasanpolje at the time as far as interethnic relations went?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for the situation -- I mean, well, on both sides it was good. At first, we had these joint patrols and guards, that is to say, to provide security to all the inhabitants of Krasanpolje. However, I mean, when Goran Zekic was killed, he was a member of parliament -- I think it was on the 8th. 8th of May, I think. There was -- there was this fear on both sides. Ethnic Serbs because, I mean, Ljubovija was nearby, well the elderly went towards Ljubovija, that is to say, to Serbia; and as for Muslims, well, they went towards Tuzla and Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's mention of the 8th of May. Which year was this that we talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992. What is the meant is the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the military-age men leave Bratunac at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please say what the situation was in view of the population of Krasanpolje; specifically, those days in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: After what happened what happened in Bijeljina and Zvornik, I've already said that the population felt this fear, both left Krasanpolje, especially the elderly men of Muslim ethnicity asked me to transfer them to Ljubovija. However, I couldn't do that. I sent them to the Territorial Defence in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to them afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Muslim inhabitants of Krasanpolje, on the 10th of May I was informed by the TO that buses would arrive. I mean, Muslims expressed the wish to leave Krasanpolje to go to Kladanj and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 10th. In the morning, a bus came and all those who happened to be in Krasanpolje got onto the bus escorted by soldiers. They went towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened later to that population that took that bus to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, these inhabitants that set out towards Bratunac, as far as I know, most of them returned to Krasanpolje after Dayton.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any specific duties in that TO unit in terms of establishment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: First, I was platoon command; and then company commander. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was your next military assignment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for the TO Bratunac, I received an order from them towards the end of June. I should -- I mean, take Kunjerac. That is a hill above Bjelovac. And the water works for all of Bratunac was up there, and I was supposed to secure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you carry out that mission?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After that order, we took the area of Kunjerac, and we stayed there until the end of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time until the end of July 1992, were you still organisationally under the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were carrying out this task, were there any clashes with the other side?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On Saint Peter's Day on the 12th of July, Kunjerac was attacked as well and I lost a soldier then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did this attack come from against the city waterworks of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Biljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was your next assignment? Where did you receive it? And how did you move on from there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: After Kunjerac, the end of July, I was given the task to take the area at Banjevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe this in terms of cardinal points. Where is the area of Banjevici so that would be clearer to us here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The area of Banjevici is in the local commune of Kravica. I mean, Kuslata is on one side and Supotnik on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were positions of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The separation line was at Banjevici. I cannot remember exactly now the place that was in front. That was held, I mean, by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time as for carrying out this mission, were you a member of the TO or was it already the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly. For a while, we were the TO. It was the detachment first and then maybe later in September -- I cannot remember. I don't know the date exactly. Then it was reformulated, and we belonged to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any specific military duties? And what were they, if you had any?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we held the lines. We weren't the only ones at Banjevici. There were others from Kravica. I mean, there was this line that we held, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any specific duties in terms of this establishment? What were the duties that you had?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: At Banjevici, I was the company commander. Actually, in the detachment, I was the morale man, and then I was company commander when it was reformulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Until when were you involved in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I mean, as far as holding the line at Banjevici was concerned, we held it up until March. The 14th of December, there was this attack and another soldier was killed there, and then until -- March 1993, I mean. After the attack on Christmas Day, these lines were moved, and in March when this operation of returning Kravica took place, after the end, I was appointed deputy commander of the 1st Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Until when were you in that position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I held that position as deputy commander of the 1st Battalion until the 6th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, what sounds in our ears very much as the personal military history of this witness, the Chamber is fully lost as far as the relevance of this detailed evidence is concerned. Could you please keep that in mind and move on as quickly as possible to portions of the evidence which clearly show relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you come into the MUP? How did you take up duties at the MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Since there was a change-over in the public security station, the then commander Ljubisa Borovcanin went to a different duty, the chief Vuka Bogdanovic went to the Zvornik centre, and then I was proposed as the station commander, and Miodrag Jusupovic, whom we called Dragan, was proposed as the chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the police from the Bratunac police station where you were the commander during those years in the second half of 1994 and in 1995, participate in combat actions.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how was this police participation in combat organised?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: When I came, these companies were not formed. However, sometime in October 1994, pursuant to an order from the ministry, companies were formed at the level of the public security centre in Zvornik, as well as in other centres. I was appointed commander of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber at that time, in 1995, how many such companies did the Zvornik centre have? The police companies.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Four or five such companies were formed. The companies were formed from all the security stations. They were younger members, younger policemen in the 1st Company. Then in the 2nd Company, it was, according to some rating, after the 1st and then the 3rd and the 4th. And then in the 5th Company, there were older members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us where were you sent specifically as the Bratunac Police Company in 1994, late 1994 and 1995? Which combat area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My company was sent to Bandijerka first, that was near Sekovici. And then later we were at Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then when you would go to carry out your military assignments, who did you receive your orders from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: We received our orders from the public security centre in Zvornik. We belonged to that centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And was there any need for your personal training or additional training in view of the duties that you were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Since I came from the civilian force, I was sent to a course for commanders that was being given in Banja Luka in June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did you spend at the course?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Until the 8th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to deal with the period that is very important to us. When did you return to the police station in Bratunac from that training course?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I returned from the course on the 8th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what was your first specific assignment once you came back from the training course.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: When I returned on the 8th of July to Bratunac, the chief, Miodrag Jusupovic, told me that something was being done around Srebrenica, or that something would be happening around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what did he specifically tell you? What can you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Because of frequent attacks by Muslim units from Srebrenica of the lines held by the members of the Bratunac Brigade military units, an attack was expected to be carried out so that these soldiers would return to the protected area; the safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did your police station receive any specific assignments in relation to these activities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the station was concerned, until the 12th of July, our assignment was to secure and carry out police assignments, monitoring public law and order. I mean, these were purely police assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, 1995, approximately at 10.00 a.m., we received a dispatch that the 2nd Company, i.e., two platoons of the 2nd Company, had to transfer to Srebrenica in the course of the day in order to provide security. Because Srebrenica was already captured, so we were supposed to provide security, perform purely police jobs in order to prevent looting of the property in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could the witness further clarify where he performed his duties up to the 12th of July. So between the 8th and the 12th, where you said you were -- you did the ordinary police work. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked at my own police station, in Bratunac. I came back on the 8th. I rested for a day or two. I had a couple of days off. And then on the 9th or the 10th, I went back to my regular duties in the town, the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Court what were your duties practically during those several days? What was your post?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question, what his assignments was during those days: Ordinary police duties. I just was interested to know where, and he told me that it is in Bratunac town. Not outside Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's -- that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going go back for a moment to that time when you received the dispatch. For purposes of clarification, could you please tell the Trial Chamber this 2nd Company of the PJP, how many members did it have at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Including the command, there were three platoons. So that would be about 100 men. In the dispatch, it said that two platoons were to report to Srebrenica, the 2nd and the 3rd, while the 1st Platoon would remain in Zvornik with my deputy. Dzelmic [phoen], he was the deputy company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know where this platoon, the 1st Platoon of the 2nd Company of the PJP was deployed in Zvornik over those few days?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it was in the sector above Kula in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you begin to implement the order that you received in the dispatch in the morning of the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The policemen of the 2nd Company were informed that they were supposed to report to the station with all of their equipment. The staging area was the police station at 3.00 p.m. They were supposed to be ready by that time. Then at 3.00 p.m. a bus arrived that was picking up the members of the 2nd and the 3rd Platoon. These were people from Sekovici, Vlasenica, and Milici, and the bus was in Bratunac ready at 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you set off for Srebrenica that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. About a couple of hours after my policemen arrived. And the policemen who had worked in Srebrenica before the war broke out, they boarded the bus. We also had a car where Petko Pavlovic was given an assignment to -- he was the chief of the public security station in Srebrenica. That's the post he was appointed to. So his assignment was to form a station, and this assignment was also given to his deputy commander Milisav Gavric. We set off at 3.00 p.m. not towards Potocari but towards Bjelovac through Sase Zaluzje. We went down near the playing field. And at approximately 5.00 p.m., we were in front of the public security station in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were the members of the newly formed police station in Srebrenica with you headed by Petko Pavlovic as the chief and Milisav Gavric as the deputy commander of the police station? Did they also enter Srebrenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I've already said that Milisav, myself, and Petko were in the car. The others were in the bus. Members of the 2nd Company, the 2nd and the 3rd Platoon, and the policemen who had worked in Srebrenica were in the bus. However, what happened was that policeman Nenad Deronjic, who was a member of the 2nd Company, and he was also a person who had worked in Srebrenica before the war. So Nenad Deronjic, Pavle Pelemis, Sredoje Bojic, were there. Also Mladen Gligic, Darko Obrenovic, and I can't remember who the others were. There were two or three other policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to ask you about that later. I'm particularly interested in one of those names. So I would just like to ask you to explain to us who are not from that area if you go through that area, do you need to pass through Potocari?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: We took a detour. We didn't go through Potocari. This is a road that goes towards Bjelovac and then turns towards Sase and then goes down next to the playing field and that's how you reach the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, when you arrived at Srebrenica at approximately 5.00 p.m., as you said, on the 12th of July, 1995, can you describe the situation there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for the situation in Srebrenica, actually, we didn't see any civilians on the streets. There was a lot of timber or wood in front of all of the buildings. It didn't look -- Srebrenica didn't look like there were many buildings that were demolished, but it was quite filthy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any other military formations in Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: There were no military formations in Srebrenica at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And was there any fighting, any resistance, any shooting when you entered Srebrenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was quiet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could the witness explain why they didn't take the shortest route and why they made a detour when they went to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We took a different route, a round-about way, because there was an UNPROFOR base where the Muslim population was from Srebrenica, so our intention was to avoid going that way and to take this other road and to -- and to avoid Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that you wanted to avoid it. But why performing normal police duties, why would you avoid the UNPROFOR base and Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that that was the order from the centre to take that route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you don't know the reasons why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. All I knew is that we were supposed to avoid that area. Probably the reason was due to the things that were happening in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were aware that Muslims were gathering there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the station, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were any details given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Muslim population was at the UNPROFOR base. That's what we were told. And Srebrenica was empty, I mean. And that order from the centre, probably from the ministry that went to the centre, was for us to go to Srebrenica and to secure work. I mean, secure the town and the establishment of the station, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say "the ministry," which ministry are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Ministry of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But what ministry? Not Ministry of Foreign Affairs, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Ministry of Police, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, when arriving in Srebrenica, did you notice any units of the Army of Republika Srpska in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I mean, there weren't any military units. Very little -- I mean, there weren't any civilians either of Serb ethnicity. They started coming in later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, practically, what's the building that you went to when you arrived in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Srebrenica, we stopped in front of the station. The police station in Srebrenica. We didn't find anybody there. So we entered the station, and we agreed on how to proceed; how our unit was to proceed, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber what your specific task was at that point in time, as commander of the 2nd Company of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My task as the commander of the 2nd Company was to secure the town, I mean, to prevent looting, and to help the new chief, Petko Pavlovic, that is, to establish the public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could I seek clarification of one of the previous answers. I'll read to you, Witness, how it was recorded. You were asked whether were any units of the Army of Republika Srpska, and you said: "At the time, ... there weren't any military units. Very little -- I mean, there weren't any civilians either of Serb ethnicity." Now, when you said "very little," did you refer to the military presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There weren't any military formations, that is. I mean, later, later civilians of Serb ethnicity appeared. Those who wanted to return to their homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Military formations. Does that mean that there was no soldier in Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In town, where we were? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you embark upon the realisation of the task that you received? What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I mean, with a few policemen, first we toured the main street from the playing field down there, to up there, where the exit is towards Zeleni Jadar. We set up two check-points. We left a police presence by the playing field. And on the exit towards Petrici. I mean, the cultural centre up there, that exit. And then this patrol that patrolled that part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How many policemen were these two check-points according to the assignments that you gave them?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember right now, but I think there were seven or eight of them. In order to be on the safe side, we assigned more policemen to every one of these check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the other policemen from the 2nd Company? What were their specific tasks in terms of implementing the task that you had received?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The other policemen were on the ready together with me in case we needed to intervene so that we could intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what the specific tasks were of the members of the newly established police station in Srebrenica on that day and on the following days?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It was already evening by then, and we had this list of policemen, and that is where the schedule is made for the 13th, so then they were supposed to establish the station and start opening documents, and a duty service was set up, and also the patrol service that is correct patrolled the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally, on that afternoon, the 12th, did you tour the town of Srebrenica when these two check-points were placed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the playing field, and I went up there towards Petrici, towards Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice something characteristic, something unusual, something that remained in your memory?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the exit towards Petrici, there is this curve. We came across a male corpse. Most probably this was an ethnic Muslim. The man was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do with the body, if you did anything specific?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: We couldn't have done anything on that day since it was already evening, but it was the following day or two days later, the civilian protection -- I mean, they had been informed, and they removed the corpse.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you notice what the cause of death had been of that particular individual?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. Because the corpse was already decaying, and we felt the stench, and I could not see from the car what the cause of death was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when touring Srebrenica, were you in a position to see whether there were any buildings that had been destroyed due to shelling?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for the town itself, I said at the very beginning that I did not notice any major destruction. I think there was this one crater by the school, at the playing field there. I didn't see any destroyed buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the members of the civilian protection did with that body, the mortal remains of that person found there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't recall. At any rate, they removed the body from that place. Most probably they buried the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day or on the following days, did you have an opportunity to see civilians of Muslim ethnicity anywhere in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: When walking around town with the police, in a basement we found a woman who was an ethnic Muslim. She could not move. Her mobility was impaired. And elderly people like that were found in cellars, basements, and they expressed the wish for us to transfer them to Potocari. We took a truck, I think it belonged to the public cleaning service, and I ordered Bojic and Obrenovic to transfer them to Potocari, and that what they did. Upon returning, they told me that they handed them over to the UNPROFOR base in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber to the best of your recollection what day that could have been? The first day you arrived? The second day after you arrived? Do you have any sense of time in that way?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the first day. That is to say, when touring the main street. That is to say, the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any pressure? Was there any abuse? Was there any mistreatment of these civilians that you found in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as the police was concerned, we really did our job. They expressed their wish to go, and we had these orders, stating that those who wished to leave, that we should transfer them to the base in Potocari. So the six or seven of them, all of them, expressed that wish. They said they wanted to go to the base, and that's where they went and that's where they stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where did you spend the night between the 12th and 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The night? Well, I mean, since there were these shifts, I mean, those who were at the check-points -- Petko and Milisav spent the night at the station. There was this apartment above the station. It belonged to a lady who worked with my wife, and that's where we spent the night. We just sat there. We didn't really sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The check-points, did they function that night; and these patrols? The night between the 12th and the 13th.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And we received no information whatsoever about any kind of problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems to me that it's time for the break now, and then I will move onto the 13th of July and what happened on that day. Perhaps this would be the right time to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break now. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, there was a matter you wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. The Court may recall that this was a matter raised at the end of the day on Thursday. It concerned two documents which had been inadvertently omitted from the list of exhibits to be potentially used in cross-examination, so Mr. Traldi refrained from tendering them at that time pending a discussion with the Defence. The Defence expressed no objection to those documents being tendered, and so we asked at the end of the day on Thursday for 65 ter 02780 and 65 ter 18494 to be admitted. And I'm repeating that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 02780 will be Exhibit P7299. And 65 ter number 18494 will be Exhibit P7300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7299 and P7300 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, could you please tell us what your specific duty was in relation to the protection of movable property in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for my unit, that is to say, the 2nd and 3rd Platoons, our task was to prevent movable property from being taken out of Srebrenica, to establish check-points, and if goods reached the check-points, then they were taken away from the persons who were carrying them. These goods would then be placed in storage where war booty was kept. So if goods were taken away at Zuti Most, they were handed over to the storage facility in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Those days, midday of the 13th, the 14th, the 15th, did Serb refugees from Srebrenica start coming into town?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I've mentioned that on the 13th there were very few of them, but on the 14th and 15th, all of those who had property there came to see what it was like. Already on the 13th, 14th, the town was already full of Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you come across situations when movable property was being unlawfully seized?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was quite a bit of that. We even had problems with people drawing weapons at us. So a few men in uniforms with a truck took some furniture or something, and we stopped that truck. It was coming from the department store and moving towards the station. We stopped them. They protested. And at one moment as I was asking for reinforcements, since I saw that there would be a problem, one of these men put a gun to my forehead. He said he'd kill me. And I said, "Okay, I'll call the chief the centre, Dragomir Vasic, and if he allows it then no problem." Then I called him, he came, and I took off my belt and I said, "I cannot take all of these goods, there would be major problems." I really could not take that situation any longer. I particularly disliked being held at gunpoint. I asked this man to leave aside his weapon if we were supposed to deal with each other. Then I said, "Let's fight bare fisted," and that's what happened. And then the chief took over the case, and then I went over to Bratunac, and what happened afterwards I don't know. So that was in the afternoon of the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Objectively speaking, with the number of men you had and the newly established police station in Srebrenica, could you make sure that all of these things could not be taken out of Srebrenica? Did you have enough personnel to secure that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. It was just the route towards Zeleni Jadar and another one, and then we had to provide security for vital facilities, like the court-house, the post office, so we didn't have enough manpower to resist all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies. I could raise this in cross-examination, but just while we're on the topic, the answer to the previous question one further up was ambiguous, where the witness said "let's fight bare fisted and that's what happened," it was ambiguous to me as to whether he meant they had that discussion or whether there, in fact, was some kind of fist fight. And I was just wondering if it would be easier to clear that up now as opposed to raising it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will you follow the suggestion of Mr. Gillett, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I think that the witness actually said so and maybe it didn't get into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, would you just please tell us what happened when you told this person who had drawn a weapon and pointed it at you to drop the weapons and to fight it out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just please repeat the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you what happened once you asked this person that was taking all these goods to drop the weapon and that you two fight it out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he -- when all of this was happening, I mean, the atmosphere was tense until Vasic arrived, the chief of the centre. Once he arrived, I explained what was happening. I dropped my belt and I said I'm going to fight him, physically. I don't want us to deal with it by drawing our weapons. And then at that point of time I hit him, I felled him to the ground, and then the chief took us to the -- aside and we talked. The chief then ordered that the truck should be escorted to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned at one point members of the newly formed police station in Srebrenica, among them Nenad Deronjic. How long have you known Nenad Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I have known Nenad Deronjic from the time I came to the Bratunac police station from the 6th of June, 1994. Because he was a member of the police station in Bratunac. Nenad Deronjic was then in my unit, in the 2nd Company, from the Bratunac security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you see him for the first time when he was performing his duties in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for Nenad Deronjic, together with the rest, because he was informed that he had to go with the rest of the 2nd Company, he was on the bus, he came together with the other members of the unit to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you have the opportunity to see Deronjic the next day, on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think that since he was a senior, experienced policeman, that he and Gavric had the task of making the schedule for the public security station service and to assign policemen at check-points and on patrol duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did you specifically remain in the town of Srebrenica on this assignment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I think that I stayed for about seven or eight days. After the 12th, I was returned to Bratunac with the unit, and then those from my unit who were from Srebrenica originally - like Nenad Deronjic - stayed behind; whereas, we returned. And then after a few days off, we went to our next assignment where the unit was as signed to Treskavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And where did you sleep during those days while you were on assignment in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The first night we slept above the police station. This was an apartment that belonged to a friend of my wife's. And on the following day, together with Sredoje Bojic and members of the Bratunac police that were in my company, we slept in the Domavija hotel and we were securing that area, the exit towards Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber where Hotel Domavija is located for purposes of transcript?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Hotel Domavija is just above the cultural hall and the church. It's in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, could you please tell us which town?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the town of Srebrenica. I am located in Srebrenica at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did any policemen sustain any injuries or were any policemen killed during those days?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No one from my unit had any such problems. As for members of my police station, on the 13th, after midnight, a member of the 1st Company - we used to call him Tulo - was killed on the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje, near Sandici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'd like to seek clarification of one of the answers. Witness, you told us what happened on the 13th of July in the afternoon, that you were threatened, and when the chief took over, you said you went over to Bratunac. At the same time, you told us that you stayed for some six, seven, or eight days in Srebrenica. Now, did you return to Bratunac in the afternoon of the 13th of July; and, if so, when did you then return to Srebrenica again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a misunderstanding. It wasn't I who went to Bratunac. That whole group of men who had resisted the seizure of the items together with the chief centre and his group went to Srebrenica. I remained in Srebrenica. And then on the 13th, we slept at the Domavija have hotel in Srebrenica. That was near the town centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know what happened with the goods which were on the truck? Whether they finally were handed over or whether they remained in the possession of those transporting them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The goods were in Bratunac. They were seized in Bratunac, the goods, and then they were placed in the building allocated for war booty.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a building of the sawmill, the 9th of October sawmill. It was a large building, so all the goods that were seized, all the war booty, was stored there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you're also recorded as having said and then the chief took over the case, and then you said they -- they were escorted to Bratunac. And you then said: "... and what happened afterwards, I don't know." What didn't you know? What did you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember the measures that were taken by the centre chief in relation to those people other than seizing the goods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you have any other more detailed information about how this policeman was killed, the one that you mentioned a little bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As for the 1st Company of the PJP, it was attached to the detachment of the deputy commander of the detachment Ljubisa Borovcanin, and as far as I know they secured the road; that is to say, Sandici towards Konjevic Polje. And at that moment, a group of Muslims came. There was gun-fire and Zeljko Ninkovic, nicknamed Tulo, was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no personal knowledge about that. It's just what you heard. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wasn't there. I only heard that in the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, it may be important to rely primarily on direct observation of witnesses rather than what was told at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the burial of that member of your police station?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber when that was, what day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the 14th of July, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, did you stay in Bratunac or did you return to Srebrenica to continue your mission?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: For those seven or eight days that I was there, I was in Srebrenica. I slept in Domavija hotel. However, every evening we had to change rooms. Because there were fleas and everybody complained about fleas, so we had to change rooms every evening to avoid being bitten.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During those seven or eight days from the 12th of July, 1995, while you were in Srebrenica, were there any units of the VRS in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were no army units in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you returned to the police station in Bratunac and then until the end of the war, what were your specific tasks?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Up to 1997, I was the commander of the police station. And then for a year I was the chief of the public security station in Bratunac. From 2008 to 2001, I worked in the police department in the Zvornik Security Services Centre. I was an inspector in the police department there. In 2001, I returned to Bratunac where I assumed the position of chief. And then when the police forces were reformed, I was appointed as the police station commander and I stayed there until the 6th of June, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this for the following reason. In 1996, did you have any specific tasks relative to the establishment of the truth about the events that took place in July in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1996, it was cold and there was frost on the ground. So I supposed that it was sometime in the winter. I was informed that Mrs. Elisabeth Rehn would come to Bratunac. The police station was supposed to provide security for her. Together with the municipal authorities and the then president Miroslav Deronjic, we were supposed to inspect the area around Bokcin Potok because there were rumours about a lot of killed Muslims there, that there had been a skirmish the previous night between the two groups of them because they didn't know of each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the police station, who gave you that task?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: From the security services centre in Zvornik, we received that task to be at the disposal of Miroslav Deronjic who be would a member of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your specific task during Mrs. Rehn's visit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: My task was to provide security for her in the perimeter around Bokcin Potok that they desired to inspect. This is what I did. I was with a couple of other police officers. I escorted Mrs. Elisabeth Rehn and there were a number of other policemen who deployed in the general sector of Bokcin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, what did you personally observe?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: We travelled by cars to a certain place. I can't remember its name. And then we continued on foot. Because Bokcin Potok is a place where you -- which you can't reach by car. We went on foot for a kilometre or so. And in that area, I observed a lot of terrible things. There were a lot of corpses, parts of bodies. I suppose that they had been dismembered by wild beasts. I can't remember how many corpses there were, but there were a lot of them and they were all decomposing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, did you provide security for anybody else; for example, people who collected the body parts or who were engaged in the sanitization of the area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, not on that occasion. Ms. Rehn inspected the area, some photos were taken, and then returned. Later on we received an order to provide security for a commission. The commission was headed by Masovic. They were in charge of collecting those body parts in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I would like to seek clarification of one of the previous answers. When you started talking about Elisabeth Rehn's visit, you said, and I read it to you and I ask a few questions about it: "... because there were rumours about a lot of killed Muslims ..., that there had been a skirmish the previous night." Was that the night before Elisabeth Rehn arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. What I meant was in July 1995, and Ms. Rehn arrived 1996. Towards the end of that year in October when it was already cold and there was frost on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said there was rumours about a skirmish between the two groups of them. Do you mean two groups of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because that probably happened during the night. That was the main passage towards Tuzla. It's a canyon and I suppose one group arrived earlier. They wanted to take a rest. The other group arrived, they thought that there was an ambush awaiting them, fire was opened, and they killed each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any personal knowledge about it or is it just that you're reproducing what you heard as rumours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have any personal knowledge of that. Obviously I didn't -- I did not participate in all that. Those are rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That next task, to secure the members of the federal commission for searching missing persons, who gave you that task?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: A dispatch came from the Security Services Centre. As uniformed police, we provided security for the location, whereas people arrived from the public security station in Zvornik. Actually, there was just one inspector who arrived and there were members of the commission from the Federation and from Republika Srpska who were also secured by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the police officers of your police station, did you accomplish that mission?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not only in that area, but also in the general area of the passage or of that road. On a number of locations we had to provide security upon the order of the Security Services Centre while the members of the commission worked in those locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the police officers from your police station, after completing the task of securing Bokcin Potok and the collection of those bodies, did they report to you about the accomplishment of the task?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Every time when security had been provided for a location, a report had to be written. But they did not have access to the location itself. They had to secure the general area so that the members of the commission could work. So they did not have the information about the number of the body parts and bodies that had been collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to the body parts that had been collected?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: According to the information that I had, they were transported to the Federation. The federal commission transported them to the Federation. I believe that they were taken in the direction of Visoko. That's where they were taken, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn from the police officers who had been given that task what was the approximate number of the bodies that were collected in Bokcin Potok?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: There were just rumours, and according to those rumours over 300 bodies were found in that area. Not only in Bokcin but also in the general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody obstruct the work of the commission? And I mean the government of the -- Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were no obstructions. I suppose that the Ministry of Interior was tasked with securing the location, and we did not encounter a single problem in our job of securing the area and the persons involved in the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about that activity of collecting bodies. How long did it last, all in all?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Until the year 1998, I was chief, and while I was chief and commander, those activities took place for a week every month. Then I went to Zvornik. And then when I returned, we still assisted those people who were involved in the collection of bodies, and we still provided security for those locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that that was close to the road. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber which road was that? Where were the bodies collected? On what route?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It was the road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, this is all hearsay. He wasn't there. Do we not have better evidence for that? I mean, why would we hear this from this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this witness was there. He was in Bokcin Potok, more specifically, when Mrs. Elisabeth Rehn arrived. So my question was in respect of his own personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. He told us that they had no access to where the bodies were found. He didn't know about the numbers, et cetera. Is it just about the road and is there any dispute about that? Is that an issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not really an issue. We have established, I think, it's up to almost 900 to 1.000 surface remains in this area going up towards the path of the column through DNA and these various time-periods where groups have come in and taken up bodies. So this is part of the case. It's in Dusan Janc's report and testimony, testimony of Dean Manning, it's all laid out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Locations are not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Locations as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in issue. I wonder what we're listening to, that someone who was on that road, and I think, as a matter of fact, that the witness more or less described where it was. Now to hear again how far it was on the road. If there's detailed evidence about all of this, Mr. Stojanovic, I leave it to you for the remaining two minutes whether you want to spend more time on this or whether you would bring us evidence which sheds even more light on the events compared to what we know already from other evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There was my last question. I would like to thank Mr. Mladjenovic for his answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I believe that I have honoured the time that I said I would need for the examination of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Witness, you'll now be examined by Mr. Gillett. You'll find Mr. Gillett to your right. Mr. Gillett is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mladjenovic. I'm going to ask you some questions concerning your evidence. If there are any questions that are unclear, please let me know as we go along. Now, firstly, you were mobilised into the Bratunac TO on 17 April 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And in June 1992, the Bratunac Battalion was incorporated into the Birac Brigade of the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: In May 1992, you were located in Krasanpolje; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Krasanpolje, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you know a Nedjelko Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And was he also a member of the company of the TO in Krasanpolje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was the company commander at the beginning while I was a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And do you know Ziko Alimpic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He died seven or eight years ago. He's a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And he was also located in Krasanpolje in May 1992 with your company; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. Because he was old. He was not in the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did he subsequently join the company after May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, our task was to be on that village watch from to Kraula to Jovankici. That's the name. Now, I really cannot remember. I mean, I know that he was over 70. At the time, I don't think that he was within the company itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What about Golub Alimpic, Ziko's son? Was he in Krasanpolje at that time as part of the company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. And I think that he was in the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, on 10 of May, 1992, Krasanpolje was attacked by Serb forces; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Not attacked. Rather out of fear, because of what was going on on the 9th of May in Glogova and the 5th, the killing of Goran Zekic, I've already spoken about that, the Muslims asked to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter document 32410.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we look at that, you started your answer by saying: "Not attacked. Rather, out of fear..." Now, these are two different things. Whether you attack someone because you are attacking him out of fear or out of aggressivity, whatever, but was there an attack by Serb forces; that is, was armed force used against that village on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness start his answer again. We did not hear a few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could you please start your answer again because the interpreters missed a few words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of what happened concerning the death of Goran Zekic and then Glogova, I mean, the locals who were Muslims, ethnic Muslims, they asked to leave the village, and they went to the municipality of Bratunac. And then on the 10th, I mean, they sent this bus, and there was this other group, I mean, of soldiers, at the station in Krasanpolje. They gathered there. Some had left earlier. Left the village earlier. Ran away. Probably out of fear. I don't know. The bus was boarded by men, women, and children. That is to say, the bus was full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I am asking you whether armed force was used against that village and its inhabitants. So could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, force had not been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you didn't hear any shooting or you didn't see anyone being threatened by arms, even without shots being fired. No use or threat of weapons was used on that day against the village and its inhabitants. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the area where I was, no, there wasn't any shooting and there were no threats. I mean, they went because they had asked to leave the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did you hear that there was any shooting in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: After the departure, yes. I mean, after the departure of the bus that left with the local inhabitants of Muslim ethnicity. Yes, there was shooting in the evening. All of that out of fear, that somebody had stayed on from the direction of Glogova so that there would not be an attack from the direction of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who was the shooting coming from, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbs. Because, I mean, well, most had weapons on both sides. So after these people left, the Serbs were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So there was shooting in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992 by the Serbs, but you maintain there was no attack or use of armed force in the village. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: There wasn't shooting. I mean, it's only natural. These soldiers who came with the bus, they were armed. I mean, there wasn't any shooting when they were getting out. I mean, these Muslims who wished to leave. And there weren't that many of them and they all wanted to leave. So that was that bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. It was: "So there was shooting in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992 by the Serbs, but you maintain that there was no attack or use of armed force in the village. Is that your position?"

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, later when they left. It was in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask for clarification. When the Serbs were shooting, what or whom were they shooting at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the evening, I mean, these village guards, watches continued, and that's when the shooting happened. They were firing into the air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at 65 ter document 32410, this is a statement dated 7 July 1992 from a Muslim resident of Krasanpolje. And if we go to page 2 of B/C/S and English, we see that he states the following: "On 9 May 1992, there was nothing particular going on, only for Krasanpolje, Dzafici and Lonjin to then be surrounded the following day, 10 May 1992, in the morning hours, by the Serb TO of Bratunac, who were opening fire towards the said villages without any reason, chasing the inhabitants off towards the bus station in Krasanpolje. The gathered inhabitants, whom there were 3- to 400 of, were driven off in two buses to the football pitch in Bratunac. "When the inhabitants were being gathered, the territorials were also carrying out the looting and torching of houses and outbuildings in Krasanpolje and Dzafici and so, therefore, in connection with that, I claim that I saw how the houses and outbuildings of the following were torched ..." He then lists people whose houses were torched. And I note for the record in the English, the name of the village is written as "Krasnopolje" but in the B/C/S original it's "Krasanpolje." Sir, there were houses of Muslims burnt down in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992; correct.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, no way. 300, 400 Muslims on two buses? That they could all fit in? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus on the question. The question was: Were houses of Muslims burned down in Krasanpolje on the 10th of May. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 10th of May, no. Later, yes, because it was impossible to protect them. During the night they were burned. That is to say, after these Muslims left. Not on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you claiming that the houses were burnt on the night of 10 to 11 May. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The 9th and later. And then the 10th, during the day, no. Well, I mean, there is this house that belongs to Bosniaks right next door to my parents' house in Krasanpolje and that was not torched. So we could not control this and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, the question is whether houses were torched. The question was not whether all Muslim houses were torched. So could you please tell us whether Muslim houses were torched evening of the 10th of May, the night from the 10th to the 11th. Could you tell us whether that happened or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't only the evening of the 10th that the torchings took place. During the month that followed, some houses were torched. I mean, most were either destroyed or ... but not on that day, the 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you said not only in the evening of the 10th. And then you said: Most were destroyed but not on the -- on that day, the 10th. How many houses approximately were torched on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 10th during the day, no. In the evening --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the evening, as far as I know, one of these houses, a house belonging to the Avdics that is close to this Golub Alimpic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And how many houses were burnt, were torched in the following days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember that right now, but this did happen. During the night, they were torched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Muslims were also killed on 10 May 1992 in Krasanpolje, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, not on the 10th. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you saying you're not sure whether Muslims were killed on 10 May 1992, or you know that they were not killed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: That part where I was, no. No, they were not killed on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask for clarification. On what date do you -- were they killed if they were not killed on the 10th of May, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, as far as I know -- I mean, all of these who were on the 10th -- I mean, the bus left and then, I mean, at the end of the war they returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, my question was: You say, no, they were not killed on the 10th. My question to you is: According to you, on what day were they killed, if they were killed at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Krasanpolje, no. Not on that day. Not later. Because already after the 10th, there weren't any in Krasanpolje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Earlier than the 10th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Before the 10th, no. I mean, before the 8th we didn't even have any of these problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, in the statement we have in front of us, various individuals are listed as killed, including, Hasid Demirovic, aged around 70 years old. He was killed on 10 May 1992, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Demirovic? I don't think he lived in Krasanpolje, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Hasan Demirovic. He was listed as being mentally handicapped. He killed on 10 May, 1992, in Krasanpolje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we go to page 3 of the English of the statement, we see that the statement maker lists the perpetrators that participated in these crimes and included amongst them he mentions Slavoljub Mladjenovic. He says: "He was one of the platoon commanders." You were a platoon commander of the TO in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992, weren't you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this statement at this stage. And I see we're coming close to the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are approximately at the time for the break. Any objections? No objections. Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Gillett, I was just wondering, I don't know how you'll continue, but in view of the last few questions, I would not have been surprised if you would have asked for a 90(E) warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
