utterances.text: Yes. Apologies. That is something I should have raised for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we leave it to the parties. Because -- but the parties know what questions will be asked and the Chamber doesn't know in advance. But now I do not know whether after the break we'll continue with similar questions, because then I would still do it. Otherwise, I would retrospectively I would still inform the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I think to be safe it is wise to inform the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, a question was asked to you, and one of the possible answers -- or at least it touches upon the possibility that a truthful answer might incriminate yourself and for that reason I would like to read to you Rule 90 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. It reads: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Is that rule clear to you, that if by giving a truthful answer you might tend to incriminate yourself, that you can ask me to refrain from answering that question and asking -- seeking permission for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That rule applies for any question that was put to you already. I don't know whether retrospectively you would seek to be relieved from an answer to the question, and I especially had in mind after it was read to you that someone gave, I think, your name as one of voluntary perpetrators, that a question was asked whether you were in a certain position at that time similar to the one that witness had mentioned. If you want to withdraw that answer or if you want to seek permission to not have answered that question, you have an opportunity to do so, and the Rule applies for any future question that will be put to you after the break. I hear, at this moment, no further comment. So we leave it to that. We'll take a break. You may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, before the break, you mentioned that the villagers from Krasanpolje moved out because of what happened had to Zoran Zekic and events in Glogova. Now, you know who Miroslav Deronjic is; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you know he pleaded guilty in relation to events in Glogova on 9 May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know how he pleaded. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can we get P3566. And this is a statement from Miroslav Deronjic where he describes events in Glogova. If we can go to page 20 in English, paragraph 106, which is pages 29 to 30 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the witness know -- Do you know about the conviction of Mr. Deronjic, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may not be familiar with the technicality of a guilty plea but apparently he is aware of Mr. Deronjic being convicted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: At paragraph 106, Miroslav Deronjic states the following: "As stated in the database, during the attack on Glogova and while the operational objective goal of the plan was being carried out to move the Muslims out permanently from Bratunac municipality, the inhabitants of Glogova, mostly women and children, were forcibly moved out of Glogova. As a result of the attack on the village of Glogova on 9 May 1992, 65 Bosnian Muslims inhabitants of the village, were killed, the entire Muslim population was moved out by force and a large number of Bosnian Muslim homes were levelled. The mosque was also torched and destroyed." Sir, these are the events in Glogova that you referred to earlier in your testimony from May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No I did not testify about Glogova. I testified about --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the last word.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last word. You testified about what, if not about Glogova?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the village of Krasan, but I mentioned Glogova because the Muslims from Krasanpolje asked to move out from their village because -- on the account of the events in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's how Mr. Gillett understood it, and that's what he put to you, and I think the question has now been answered, whether these are these events. When you refer to Glogova, you refer to the events as was just read out by Mr. Gillett reflecting what the statement of Mr. Deronjic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, on 12th of July, when you came into - and this is 1995 - when you came into Srebrenica as the commander of the PJP, you said that you took a tour of the town; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The main street that leads from the football pitch in Srebrenica towards Bratunac, i.e., from the road leading from Sase up to the exit towards Zeleni Jadar, that main road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you said during this tour you saw a male dead body that you said was most probably Muslim. On what basis did you consider the body was "most probably Muslim"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I concluded that because the body had been left lying there. If he had been a fallen Serbian soldier, whoever was with him would have probably taken him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Was Nenad Deronjic with you when you took this tour around the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. There were a couple of policemen. We were in a car, a Golf 2 car, a grey car, a police vehicle from Bratunac. The five of us came in it including Miroslav. I used that car as commander, and I used that car when I toured the village. I can't remember the policemen who were in the car on that specific occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say your recollection concerning Nenad Deronjic is vague around that period of time in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, Nenad Deronjic was on the bus together with Miroslav Gavic, and he was tasked with scheduling the departures. I guarantee that Miroslav [As interpreted] Deronjic was in Srebrenica both on the 12th and on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: When you saw this dead body on the evening of the 12th, as commander of the PJP present, did you investigate the causes of death of this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. My task was just to secure the location. When the police station was established, criminal police inspectors were supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: A second ago, on the transcript, it appeared to say "I guarantee that Miroslav Deronjic was in Srebrenica on the 12th and the 13th." I take it you meant Nenad Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Nenad Deronjic, not Miroslav Deronjic. Nenad Deronjic. He was a policeman in the 2nd Company. Miroslav Deronjic was not in Srebrenica with us. He was a member of the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And you said you did not investigate how this person died on the evening of the 12th but that criminal police inspectors were supposed to do that. Do you know if they actually did investigate how this person died?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. You have to ask Petko Pavlovic. He was the then chief of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now you claimed earlier today at temporary transcript page 26 that you saw Nenad Deronjic on the 13th of July, 1995. Where did you see him, specifically?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: In the police station in Srebrenica. He was on duty. The police station had already been established. The duty service had already been established, and he was on duty as the duty officer at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What time of the day was that on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the entire day. Throughout the entire day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So your evidence is that he was in the police station throughout the entire day - and I'm referring to Nenad Deronjic - on 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get Exhibit D588 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And while this is coming up, this is the Srebrenica log-book for the police station. Now, if we go to page 2 of the English and B/C/S, we see that it's dated 12 July. And that's you assigned as working in the police station at the top; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And then if we --

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Here this could be only for the 13th because on the 12th at 5.00 we were in Srebrenica, so it's possible that this refers to the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So are you disputing that you were at work at the police station as reflected here on 12th July? And I should note it's our understanding this is the Srebrenica log-book.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that this does not refer to the 12th. I was helping with the station when it came to the establishment of the station, and I also assisted at the check-points. So this cannot be -- or, rather, it can be, because -- I apologise. 19 -- yes. Between 1900 and 0700 in the morning, so we're talking about the night between the 12th and the 13th. So, yes, this is plausible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we continue on a page, to the next page in B/C/S and English, and if we can rotate the B/C/S and zoom in -- yes, on the left side. Here we see for the 13th of July, 1995, that again you're listed as working in the police station. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I worked at the police station and I also worked with my own unit. I assisted the people in the station, the deputy commander who been appointed and who was in charge of the establishment of the police station in Srebrenica, and I also secured the check-points together with the members of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So the notation next to your name, 07 to 07 hours, that means that you were on duty for 24 hours from 7.00 a.m. on 13 July through to 7.00 a.m. 14th July; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Everybody had the same schedule. They were on duty for the same duration of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So when you say you secured the check-points together with the members of the 2nd Company, does that mean you were not physically located at the police station throughout that 24-hour period?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was not physically present. I came to the police station as necessary to be briefed. On the 13th, the 14th, and on the other days or at nights I slept in Domavija. There was an UNPROFOR warehouse there, and we also secured that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So if you were not present at the police station throughout 13 July 1995, how could you state, as you earlier stated, that you were with Nenad Deronjic at the police station in Srebrenica throughout 13 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Not the entire day. However, he was on duty, and whenever I popped over, I saw him. He was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So when you answered my question at transcript page 50, my question was: "So your evidence is that he was in the police station throughout the entire day - and I'm referring to Nenad Deronjic - on 13 July 1995?" And you said: "Yes, yes." That was, in fact, not correct. He was not present at the police station throughout the entire day, was he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever I popped in the police station, Nenad was there. As a person on duty, he had to be. And in my absence, and that absence never lasted five hours, for example, I would go to the check-points and then I would return to the police station, and whenever I returned to the police station, Nenad was there. I saw him, I announced my presence, I asked him to see the chief, and so on and so forth. It was Nenad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could go one further page on in this exhibit, which is D588.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We see at the top that Nenad Deronjic is listed as being on security at Domavija and Drina, I understand that's the Domavija hotel, and is not listed throughout the day as being present at the Srebrenica police station, is he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: What date is this? I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: This is a continuation of the assignments for 13 July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: If he was scheduled to provide security, then he was. I can't remember exactly. We're talking about the 14th effectively? Or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, your recollection is vague in relation to --

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: -- Nenad Deronjic's location on 13 July 1995, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. I know exactly that he was in Srebrenica. Whenever I popped in the police station, I found him there on duty as the duty police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, sir, you yourself claim to have left Srebrenica on 13 July 1995, and we'll see this if we go to 65 ter document 1D5360.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that. Witness, here, in the sequence of this document, Mr. Deronjic, N. Deronjic, is reported as having played in a role of security of Domavija and Drina between 7.00 in the morning and 7.00 in the evening. Do you have any explanation as why he is here reported as not being at the police station, whereas you said I always saw him there, whenever you popped in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the 13th, whereas this here supposedly covers the 14th and the 15th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it does not. That's your -- you have invented that. This is the following page - and I take it that there's no page left out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If I may. This was addressed last time D588 was used, and the Prosecution at the time used 65 ter document 30998 because there is a page of the English translation missing. But when you look at the B/C/S and the English, it is perfectly clear that this is a continuation of 13 July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The missing English translation does not change the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And has the missing English translation, is now part of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: No. And I could suggest, obviously it's a Defence exhibit, that if there was no objection, we could replace this version of D588 with 65 ter document 30998 to avoid any ambiguity whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm -- I think if the parties could agree on that, we would hear from the results of that. And let's focus exclusively on -- that the B/C/S version. It's just names and times. And -- Witness, this is -- the Prosecution claims that this is just the 13th of July, and perhaps we could go back one page if these are sequential pages. You see here Mr. Deronjic being reported security of Domavija from 7.00 in the morning until 1900 hours in the afternoon. And could we go back for one page. There, also for the 13th of July, I see Mr. N. Deronjic is reported as on duty service from 9.00 in the evening until 7.00 in the morning. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I believe it says 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 19, yes, yes, I mean 19. So according to this document, Mr. Deronjic was only in the evening, on from 7.00, supposed to work in the police station; whereas, from 7.00 in the morning until 7.00 at the evening, he is supposed to have worked providing security for Domavija. Do you have any comment on the -- this document compared to you telling us that whenever you popped in during the day of the 13th, that you always saw Mr. Deronjic in the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 13th, Deronjic was in the police station. I'm sure of that. Gavric and him were in charge of working on the schedule. In the course of that day, whenever I popped over at the police station I saw him there. On several occasions I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're repeating your testimony rather than giving an explanation, which you may not have. Mr. Gillett, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Then we would just note if we again go further one page in the B/C/S original, and given this witness's evidence which he has repeated, I'm not going to belabour the point, but we see that the numbers beside Nenad Deronjic's name have been altered in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you see that those numbers have been altered, sir?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: It says here from 0900 to 1900. As far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: My question wasn't what you think it says. It was that the numbers have been altered. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I can't confirm that things have been altered. I can only see that they have been made bolder.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll move on. Sir, if we could get 65 ter document 1D5360, and this is your statement originally given to the Karadzic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could go to paragraph 33, which should be page 9 of the English; page 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And here, sir, at paragraph 33, you claim: "In the morning hours of 13 July 1995, I was informed over the radio that the night before our policeman Zeljko Ninkovic had been killed. Zeljko was a member of the 1st Company and they were in Sandici providing security for the road. He was killed by Muslims, who had attacked the police in that sector before dawn. I went to the funeral in Bratunac that day and returned to Srebrenica in the evening." According to your own statement to the Karadzic Defence, you were not even in Srebrenica throughout the day of 13 July 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: There's a mistake here. On the 13th, I condoled the family and then I returned. The burial, however, was on the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: There were condolences for the family on the 13th and that was outside of Srebrenica town, wasn't it, where the family was located?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they resided in Bratunac. Family Ninkovic resided in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you did leave Srebrenica town to go and condole the family on 13 July 1995. That's your evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can just have a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, in your evidence earlier, you mentioned a dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could get document P2111.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And, first, sir, one of the platoons of the 2nd PJP Company was located in Konjevic Polje on 13 July 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: 2nd Company, my company? Is that what you mean? No. The 1st Platoon of my company was in Zvornik at Kula Grad, and the platoon commander was with them Dzelmic [phoen], the deputy commander of my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, if we now look at this dispatch, we'll see it's from the chief of the CJB of Zvornik. Now, that was Dragomir Vasic at that time; right? Sir, just -- not looking at the document, could you confirm that the chief of the CJB Zvornik at that time was Dragomir Vasic? This is in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we now look at paragraph 5 of this dispatch, which is on page 1 English and page 2 of the B/C/S, and I apologise, the B/C/S is slightly faded but we'll do our best. It states: "Acting upon the President Karadzic's order which was conveyed to us today over the phone, the 2nd Company of the Zvornik PJP, (two platoons-60 men) shall be dispatched to Srebrenica with a task to secure all facilities of vital importance in the town, at all the [sic] costs and protect them from looting and misappropriation." Sir, that's the assignment of your members of your PJP to Srebrenica town on 12 July; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It then goes on to sate: "It will carry out the task without co-operation of military police which is busy with other tasks. A platoon of this company will lie in ambush at Ravni Buljim, since the Muslim groups were spotted fleeing along the [sic] axis." Ravni Buljim is not Kula Grad. These are separate locations; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's in the area of Bratunac. But there's no chance that anyone of my platoons was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Ravni Buljim is located between Jaglici and Konjevic Polje, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It belongs to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we now look at 65 ter document -- sorry, Exhibit P6687. And this is a bulletin from the Zvornik public security centre for 13 and 14 July 1995. If we look at page 2 of the English and B/C/S, under point number 5, we see that it states: "Due to infiltration of enemy military formations from Srebrenica into the zone of the Zvornik CJB and areas of Konjevic Polje, Cerska, Han Pogled, Dzafin, Kamen, Snagovo, Maricici, and other places at risk, the 1st, 2nd, 5th, and 6th Companies of the Zvornik CJB are engaged. In co-ordinated action with the police from Doboj, Bijeljina, and Pale, as well as the VRS, they are laying ambushes." Sir, members of the 2nd PJP company were engaged in combat operations in areas including Konjevic Polje on 13 and 14 July; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. No chance that they participated. My two platoons were in Srebrenica. And this is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions in re-examination, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll start with the last document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Mr. Mladjenovic, for the record, this is document P6687. The information contained in paragraph 5, Dzafil Kamen, Snagovo, Maricici, do they say anything to you? Do you know where they are?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Toward Kalesija as far as I can remember, as far as I know. Kamen I don't know. Maricici, also no. Only this area of Konjevic Polje-Cerska. I know that. Han Pogled, that is above Vlasenica, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that one of your platoons from the 2nd Company was in the area of the Zvornik centre in the area of Kula, I would like to ask you to tell the Trial Chamber for the sake of clarification if you know where this area of Kula Grad is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, this 1st Platoon that was led by my deputy, Dzelmic, is above Zvornik. That is the highest point. I think that's it, Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far away is this area from the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: 20 -- about 25 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive reports? Did you know whether the 1st Platoon of your company had any combat contact with the column of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The deputy commander had to write reports to the command of the PJPs; that is to say, the centre of public security. I personally did not receive such a report because he would have written directly to the command and the centre of public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At those moments, who was he subordinated to and who does he take orders from when on such a mission?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: To the CSB and the commander of the PJPs, Danilo Zoljic. Danilo Zoljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like that we see P7301.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, where there seems to be some differences between what is found in this document and what the witness tells us, where he also tell us that reports were sent to -- to the command of the PJPs, if that documentary evidence would be available which would support the witness's testimony, of course the Chamber would -- would really appreciate if we would have those reports as well, which would perhaps strengthen the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we're working on that, and we will try to identify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P7301 then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You'll see it in front of you. I'd like to ask you whether you know a man by the name of Haris Avdic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he's a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 2 of this document, both in B/C/S and in English. In English, could we please move onto the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this statement which was put to you, he says, inter alia -- it's the last paragraph in B/C/S and the second paragraph in the English version: "Out of the persons who participated in the looting and torching I recognised among others," and now he enumerates several persons, including yourself. Your name is mentioned here. Now this is what I'm asking you: Were you at any point in time, you personally involved in the torching of anybody's house in the village of Krasanpolje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I guarantee that I was not. And I also guarantee for these young men here too. They did nothing either. Haris left with that group on the bus, and after Dayton he returned for a while. Now I don't know whether he was in the Federation or wherever. I don't know where he is. Maybe he even died.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Second question: You personally, did you participate in any way in torching anybody's house on that day in Krasanpolje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No. I stand by what I said: That I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to end with the following question: Do you have any rational explanation as for the reasons why this man, as stated here on the 7th of July, 1992, refers to your name?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know, and there's no reason. His son and I went to school together. We communicated until the very departure, so, really, there were no problems whatsoever. I socialised with his son. We were friends. There's no reason. So I was not torching.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like you to tell the Court what the physical distance is - and therefore the time distance as well - between the Domavija hotel and the building of the police station in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: 500 to 1000 metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what building that is that is called in Drina in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the forestry company. It's close to Domavija, over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how far away is that building, Drina, from the police station?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: The same basically. Perhaps some 50 metres, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic, on behalf of the Defence of General Mladic, I would like to thank you for the answers that you provided to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Mladjenovic, this concludes your -- no, I'm sorry. I should have given the opportunity to the Prosecution to put any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies to interrupt and just a further question arising from the re-exam. Further cross-examination by Mr. Gillett:

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand you to have said that none of the persons mentioned in this paragraph that we see at the bottom of the statement was involved in the crimes in Krasanpolje, but in the B/C/S, the paragraph is cut off. So I wonder if we could -- if you could look through those names and if we could scroll over the page to make sure that you've had a look at all of the names before you provide that answer.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these were members of the Territorial Defence, the Krasanpolje Platoon, and I guarantee that none of them had committed any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if we could just scroll over the page in B/C/S to give the witness a chance to see the names, just to be sure. And, sir, if you have a quick glance, do you stand by your answer that none of those individuals were involved in crimes in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need more time to read it, take your time, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I've had a look. This first part, I mean up to Nedjelko Blagojevic, I mean, they did not belong. I mean, they were in the TO in a hamlet near the village of Krasanpolje. Vido Radovic was not in Krasanpolje. He was an active-duty policeman. Then Milomir Vasic, also active-duty policeman --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, to cut you off, but my question is: Having seen these names, do you maintain that none of them could have been or were involved in crimes in Krasanpolje on 10 May 1992, or do you want to change that evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Gillett "were they" or "could they have been"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I meant "were."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by the following, that the young men from the TO of Krasanpolje did not commit any crime. As for these others that belonged to other units, I cannot say anything about them because they were not in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you've clarified that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would have one follow-up question. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that what you told us about the events on the 10th of May in that village, that you only testify about your own people? And whatever crimes may have been committed by others on that day, that you just don't know or you cannot be certain about?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by my men in the area of Krasanpolje. Now this part, Dzafici, and up there, and Brdjanini, I could not. I mean, my men were not there and I cannot say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Krasanpolje, were these exclusively your men who were there? Or were there others as well?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly how many, but there were soldiers that came on a bus from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they were all, as you call them, men in your unit?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No, no. The TO Bratunac sent an escort of soldiers. They were not from my men from the Krasanpolje Platoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think you said that they only shot in the air in the evening. Would that be true for all of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Not all. That is to say, those who were on guard duty. Well, all right. There is this possibility that there were locals, too. I mean, those who were not on guard duty, that they were firing as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you seen that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it could just be heard during the night. The shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whether they shot in the air or whether they were shooting otherwise, you wouldn't know?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that there weren't any fatalities, so I know that they were firing into the air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, sometimes you can shoot on a target and not have any fatalities. So that they were shooting in the air is just a conclusion which you drew from the fact that there were no fatalities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And on the basis of those who had guard duty, who were on guard. I mean, from the Krasanpolje Platoon. They said that they were firing into the air out of some kind of fear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, earlier in your testimony you have also referred to guard duties continuing. You remember that? Otherwise, I'll find it for you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it did continue for a while. And after that as a unit we went to the area of Bjelovac, where we, I mean, secured the public water works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. You said, answering a question of Judge Moloto, when you said: "Well, in the evening, I mean, these village guards, watches, continued, and that's when the shooting happened. They were firing into the air." The village guards, the watches that continued, could you explain what village guards you had on mind, what watches continued?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean, this platoon of mine, they continued their guard duty in Krasanpolje along the road from Karaula to Jovankici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the question put to you by Judge Moloto to which this was an answer was: "When the Serbs were shooting, what or whom were they shooting at?" And then you gave the answer: "Well, in the evening, I mean, these village guards, watches, continued ..." Which suggests that the village guards were the targets of the shooting. Or have I misunderstood that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB MLADJENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, out of fear. Rather, out of fear. I mean, it wasn't that they were firing at targets. They were firing into the air for a simple reason: Because they were afraid. They were all civilians who were engaged to be soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that. If there are no further questions for the witness, then, Mr. Mladjenovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, in view of the fact that the Prosecutor has shortened the cross-examination of the previous witness, we don't have the next witness ready now. We are only scheduled to start working with him at half past 3.00 this afternoon. Hence, we would kindly ask you to allow us not to bring the next witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness -- we are informed that the witness is there. Is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had to be cautious. Although we have not prepared him, but we asked our Case Manager to have the witness here, but we would kindly ask not to bring him into the courtroom. But we are in your hands and we are awaiting your decision, Your Honours. We would very much like to proof this witness before we bring him into the courtroom, if at all possible. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes, I'm a bit surprised because if everyone should have strictly kept to the time they scheduled, that would have been some three and a half hours, and then some time is remaining. So, therefore, I do not fully understand why you expected that there would be no time left. Because a day in court is more than three and a half hours. Let me just consult with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you could have expected that some time would be left today, as it now turns out that there is. Nevertheless, the Chamber is not insisting on you calling this witness now and that you'd rather proof him although he's a viva voce witness. So, therefore, whether one of the purposes of proofing a witness is to ask him to read his statement, if he is a 92 ter witness, apparently this is not a 92 ter witness, I take it that you fully prepared him for all that. So therefore, still with some surprises, and the Chamber will consider whether or not the time lost will be counted as time taken by the Defence, but, as I said, we still have to consider that. But we're losing more than half an hour in court. Under those circumstances, unless there's any matter left - and I may have a short matter to raise -

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: One note. In relation to the Exhibit D588 that was referred to, the Srebrenica police log-book, I'll consult with my colleagues from the Defence as to whether they're agreeable to substitute the translation with all the pages of the relevant section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the original is still available?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Yes. And the original has the relevant pages. There's one page in the English translation that was missing, and we'll consult on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it's a kind of a booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The original is right outside the courtroom, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that, Mr. Stojanovic, if it's a kind of booklet which is different from loose pages, then if there's no dispute about that, then the Chamber is not inclined to ask at this moment to inspect it ourselves. But if there's any dispute about that, we'd like to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today, at the end of the day, I would like to have a look at the document together with the Prosecutor. And if you agree, I believe that we will be able to agree on the document and then we will inform you thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would -- anticipating, however, that the parties may agree on it would like to have a look at the document, if it's just outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Certainly. And just for the record, we maintain, as mentioned earlier during the cross-examination, that there have been alterations, an alteration in particular, that I drew the witness's attention to, but I believe my colleague is obtaining the original book right now for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can have a look at that then as well. Meanwhile, I use the time to deal with a different matter, which is P3343. On 28th of January of this year, the Chamber notified the Prosecution of an extra or an erroneous page that had been included in P3343. On the 9th of February, the Prosecution notified the Chamber that a corrected version of P3343 has been uploaded into e-court under 65 ter number 30587b. I -- the Chamber has not heard of any objections. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the existing version of P3343 with document bearing 65 ter number 30587b. And, Mr. Stojanovic, if there would be any further dispute about this, then of course you can revisit the matter within the next 24 hours. Could the usher assist in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- giving the original of the exhibit to the Bench. At this moment we're not primarily interested in the translation. We take it that -- but in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. And I believe in the record earlier we referred to the relevant B/C/S page of D588 as to where we maintain that there is an alteration in relation to Nenad Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And I believe the ERN for the relevant page should be 0177-9703. If that is the page with Nenad Deronjic as the first name mentioned. If not, then it's the ERN finishing with a 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's the one finishing with a 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole ERN numbering a bit confusing, starting last three digits, 702; it's the 12th of July. Then 703 for the right-hand page, still 12th of July. Then for the 13th of July, there was originally 703 which is stricken out. Then for the next page, which is the second page also for the 13th of July, again 703 has been stricken out and has been replaced here by 704. Finally, the last page before entries made on the 14th, so still covering the 13th, there we have again 703 stricken out and replaced by 705 at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe when this came up in court previously with the relevant witness, we referred to 65 ter document 30998, and there was a -- one or two loose leafs of paper which were part of the book which may have been part of the cause of the restamping of the pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there is one loose page, 0177-9701, which is a handwritten document without a date which is in here as well. We haven't looked at that. Is it -- as far as time is concerned, has it been identified as what date this refers to, this loose page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'd have to check up on that for the loose page. But I believe in 65 ter document 30998 it is placed as the second -- the third page on e-court, and it's a list of names that's handwritten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It can be returned to the Prosecution, Mr. Registrar. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 8th of April, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of April, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
